direction: amodal completion, 3D reconstruction and 3D amodal completion
method: ARIS research-lit style gap analysis followed by idea-creator style hypotheses; no GPU experiments launched

papers.title: NOVA3R: Non-Pixel-Aligned Visual Transformer for Amodal 3D Reconstruction

paper_fact: Uses learnable scene tokens to aggregate unposed image views.
Uses a flow-matching 3D decoder to generate complete point clouds.
Evaluates scene and object completion on SCRREAM, 7-Scenes, NRGBD and GSO.
evidence_explanation: A global non-pixel-aligned representation reduces duplicated geometry because multiple views share one scene representation.
Flow matching is a better fit than nearest-neighbor Chamfer for unordered point generation in the reported ablation.
research_hypothesis: Separating observed, inferred and uncertain tokens will improve calibration of hidden geometry.
Multi-hypothesis outputs will be more honest than a single deterministic completion under severe occlusion.

papers.problem_gap: Pixel-aligned reconstruction is tied to visible rays, leaving holes and duplicated structures in overlapping views.
papers.why_method_needed: The bottleneck is the output representation, so a post-hoc hole-filling module cannot fully solve global consistency.
papers.why_may_work: Scene tokens fuse views globally; a 3D generative decoder can use shape priors to produce points without pixel supervision.
failure_conditions: Too few views or tokens for large scenes.
Dynamic objects violate the static-scene assumption.
Hidden geometry is underdetermined and may be plausible but wrong.
papers.evidence_boundary: Strong geometry evidence on the reported benchmarks; no direct evidence for long videos, UAV outdoor domain or semantic correctness of occluded surfaces.

ideas.name: Evidence-decomposed scene tokens
ideas.method: Use separate observed, inferred and uncertainty token groups and predict source labels with geometry.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Compare CD, hole ratio and confidence calibration by occlusion level on SCRREAM.
ideas.risk: Extra token groups may only add capacity.

ideas.name: Temporal NOVA3R
ideas.method: Add temporal tokens, object tokens and cross-frame 3D consistency.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Evaluate 3–5 frame inputs on synthetic dynamic scenes using jitter and hidden-region CD.
ideas.risk: Tracking errors can fuse moving objects.

ideas.name: Multi-hypothesis completion
ideas.method: Sample several point clouds and rank them by visible reprojection and cross-view consistency.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Report best-of-N CD, coverage and calibration under increasing occlusion.
ideas.risk: Diversity may be noise rather than meaningful ambiguity.

papers.title: Amodal3R: Amodal 3D Reconstruction from Occluded 2D Images

paper_fact: Targets complete 3D object reconstruction from occluded 2D observations.
Uses an object-level amodal 3D latent representation.
evidence_explanation: Direct 3D completion avoids cascading an uncertain 2D inpainting error into geometry.
The object-level prior is useful for regular shapes but can bias unusual objects toward common templates.
research_hypothesis: Explicit occluder geometry and depth ordering will improve hidden-surface recovery.
Category-agnostic structural tokens can reduce long-tail template bias.

papers.problem_gap: Single-view 3D methods often recover only visible surfaces or depend on clean object crops.
papers.why_method_needed: The target is complete object geometry, so the model must reason beyond pixels rather than only estimate visible depth.
papers.why_may_work: An object-level latent can store shape priors and infer hidden parts jointly.
failure_conditions: Cluttered scenes and incorrect object masks.
papers.evidence_boundary: Directly relevant object-level evidence; scene-level, open-world and temporal claims remain unverified.

ideas.name: Occluder-aware amodal latent
ideas.method: Condition on visible mask, occluder mask and depth order.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Stratify by occlusion ratio and compare hidden-surface CD.
ideas.risk: Depth order may be unavailable in real data.

ideas.name: Category-agnostic structural tokens
ideas.method: Disentangle category semantics from geometric structure tokens.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Train on seen categories and test on held-out categories.
ideas.risk: Disentanglement may remove useful shape priors.

ideas.name: Multi-view amodal fusion
ideas.method: Generate per-view shape hypotheses and fuse with cross-view consistency.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Measure gains from one, two and four unposed views.
ideas.risk: View association errors can create conflicting shapes.

papers.title: GENA3D: Generative Amodal 3D Modeling

paper_fact: Frames amodal 3D modeling as conditional generation.
Uses a 3D latent denoising/generative process to recover complete shapes.
evidence_explanation: A generative model can represent multiple plausible hidden shapes instead of averaging them.
Visible-region consistency is needed to prevent attractive but input-inconsistent generations.
research_hypothesis: Sampling diversity can be calibrated against hidden-region uncertainty.
Scene relation constraints can remove geometrically plausible but physically impossible completions.

papers.problem_gap: Deterministic regressors collapse multiple valid hidden shapes into one average prediction.
papers.why_method_needed: Occluded geometry is intrinsically multi-solution, so a single point estimate hides uncertainty.
papers.why_may_work: Latent diffusion provides a prior over complete 3D shapes conditioned on visible evidence.
failure_conditions: Generated diversity may not match real ambiguity.
papers.evidence_boundary: Supports generative amodal modeling at object level; requires stronger reprojection, multi-view and scene-level validation.

ideas.name: Evidence-ranked sampling
ideas.method: Rank generated shapes by visible reprojection, depth ordering and local geometry.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Compare random, likelihood and evidence-ranked selection.
ideas.risk: Ranking can favor visually conservative but incomplete shapes.

ideas.name: Diffusion uncertainty calibration
ideas.method: Map sample variance to hidden-surface error.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Evaluate calibration error across occlusion levels.
ideas.risk: Variance may reflect model noise rather than epistemic uncertainty.

ideas.name: Scene-graph constrained generation
ideas.method: Reject samples violating support, contact or occlusion relations.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Measure physical violation rate before and after constraints.

papers.title: TACO: Test-Time Adaptation for Occlusion-Robust 3D Reconstruction

paper_fact: Studies test-time adaptation under occlusion and deployment shift.
Uses unlabeled test observations to adapt a reconstruction model.
evidence_explanation: Adaptation changes the model's interpretation of the current scene; it does not create new geometric evidence.
Restricting updates to reliable visible regions is safer than adapting on all pseudo-labels.
research_hypothesis: Temporal consistency can make test-time adaptation safer for video.

papers.problem_gap: A model trained on one occlusion and sensor distribution can fail when deployment conditions change.
papers.why_method_needed: Collecting dense labels for every new domain is expensive, so the model needs a label-free adaptation path.
papers.why_may_work: Current inputs contain self-consistency signals from visible regions, views and geometry.
failure_conditions: Online updates can drift or forget the base model.
Fast motion and camera changes break consistency signals.
papers.evidence_boundary: Useful deployment principle; not evidence that adaptation alone solves 3D amodal ambiguity.

ideas.name: Confidence-gated adaptation
ideas.method: Update only from high-confidence visible regions and freeze the decoder.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Compare global, visible-only and random updates under domain shift.
ideas.risk: High-confidence regions may be systematically biased.

ideas.name: Cross-frame stable adaptation
ideas.method: Use short-window temporal consistency as a self-supervised signal.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Measure drift and reconstruction error on videos.
ideas.risk: Wrong tracking can corrupt the update.

ideas.name: Adaptation plus hypothesis selection
ideas.method: Generate several amodal candidates and select after adaptation.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Compare single prediction with best-of-N under shift.

papers.title: Occlusion-Aware Temporally Consistent Amodal Completion

paper_fact: Uses temporal information for amodal completion in videos.
Treats visible and occluded regions with different reliability.
evidence_explanation: Adjacent frames can provide extra evidence, but only when correspondence is reliable.
Occlusion-aware weighting prevents unknown regions from being forced to match a false target.
research_hypothesis: 2D temporal consistency and 3D shape consistency should be optimized jointly.
Segmenting occlusion events is better than using one temporal loss for all motion patterns.

papers.problem_gap: Frame-wise amodal predictions can flicker and change shape without physical reason.
papers.why_method_needed: Video supplies repeated observations that can constrain otherwise ambiguous hidden regions.
papers.why_may_work: Flow/tracking aligns evidence over time and stabilizes object identity and boundaries.
failure_conditions: Fast motion, camera shake or object reappearance.
Long occlusions provide no fresh evidence.
papers.evidence_boundary: Supports temporal stability; direct 3D geometry and UAV-scale scene claims need separate validation.

ideas.name: Bidirectional 2D-3D consistency
ideas.method: Jointly constrain mask tracks and 3D shape tracks.
ideas.risk: A wrong 3D estimate can contaminate the 2D track.

ideas.name: Occlusion-event segmentation
ideas.method: Use separate models for short, long and reappearing occlusions.

ideas.name: Error-propagation detector
ideas.method: Drop or reset memory when visible reprojection error rises.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Measure recovery after deliberately injected tracking failures.

papers.title: OccTTA: Fast and Memory-Efficient Test-Time Adaptation for 3D Occupancy Prediction

paper_fact: Targets test-time adaptation for 3D occupancy prediction.
Focuses on memory and speed constraints in deployment.
evidence_explanation: Occupancy adaptation addresses domain shift but does not resolve the multi-solution nature of hidden geometry.
An explicit unknown state is safer than forcing invisible voxels to occupied or free.
research_hypothesis: Unknown-aware occupancy can improve 3D amodal calibration.
Only updating tokens involved in cross-view conflicts may reduce drift.

papers.problem_gap: 3D occupancy models degrade across cities, weather, sensors and camera conditions.
papers.why_method_needed: A fixed model cannot cover every deployment domain, while dense target-domain labels are unavailable.
papers.why_may_work: Spatial continuity, multi-view agreement and prediction statistics provide label-free adaptation signals.
failure_conditions: Large spatial errors create correlated voxel mistakes.
Domain shift and real dynamics can be confused.
Online updates can damage previously learned geometry.
papers.evidence_boundary: Relevant for deployment robustness; not a direct amodal completion method.

ideas.name: Unknown-aware occupancy
ideas.method: Use visible, unknown and occupied states and calibrate unknown-to-occupied confidence.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Evaluate hidden-voxel calibration by occlusion ratio.
ideas.risk: Unknown may become a dumping class.

ideas.name: Conflict-driven adaptation
ideas.method: Update only features linked to multi-view spatial conflicts.
ideas.minimal_experiment: Compare global and conflict-local updates under weather shift.

ideas.name: Static/dynamic split
ideas.method: Adapt static occupancy while freezing dynamic object memory.
ideas.risk: Incorrect motion masks can route updates wrongly.
